Implementation Plan

I've got enough context to write the plan; nothing in the code contradicts the clarified scope (diagnostics only, the resolver stays fail-closed). One correction to the clarify answer: the new error line will change the heal fingerprint for future reports. That is expected, and it is covered below.

# Implementation plan: name the cause when the conflict resolver rejects a conflicted path (diagnostics only, still fail-closed)

**Planning ref:** `stable` at `b728d0ac545fe1c418e8c92375a848b90e27e2be` (`heads/stable`). This matches the integration-branch metadata (`stable`) and is the commit the consumer wrapper is pinned to.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends check_paths
Scope-mode justification: The clarification answers chose Q1=A and Q2=A. The resolver stays fail-closed, the `sandbox_path_unsupported` / `sandbox_path_host_only` tokens stay as they are, and nothing new is admitted to the sandbox. The change does extend the existing rejection report written by `check_paths` in `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` and the existing reader `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths` in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, so the next failure names its category. Per the Boil the Lake rule, the plan also covers the one blind spot the code shows: the check-paths wrapper exits 1 on `OSError`/`UnicodeError` without writing a report (`review_untrusted_workspace.py:590-595`). A best-effort `error<TAB><token>` line costs about 10 LOC and no new interface, so it is included (§6: Correctness & safety ranks above Speed). The actual root-cause fix waits until a later occurrence names the category, as the issue's suggested fix says.

## Mandatory automation section (§20.E)
- **New script?** No. Only existing code changes: two existing scripts, two existing test modules, plus `agents.md` and a changelog fragment.
- **Scheduler / entry point:** unchanged. The code runs where it already runs, from `review_autofix.yml` → `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, at the existing path gates (lines 2287-2291 and 2510-2515). It is staged from the verified workflow-support SHA through `REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS`, and both files are already there.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed.
- **DB work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry needed (no new script).

## Conflict detection
- The issue's "Affected files" carry a `coding-workflows/` prefix (for example `coding-workflows/scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`). The real repo-relative paths have no prefix. Implement must use the unprefixed paths listed under files_touched below, or the automation-path grant guard (`IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD`, exact `files_touched` match) will reject the commit.
- The clarify rationale for Q2 says the new line leaves the heal fingerprint unchanged. That is not quite right. `error-signature --strip-autofix-header` is led by `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_FIRST_ERROR`, which takes the first specific `::error::` line, so future reports get a fingerprint per category instead of `914b37…`. This is the intended effect. Lineage still continues on the same PR because autofix reports also dedupe by the PR's `source=` marker. The non-retryable cap is unaffected: it keys on `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON`, which does not change.
- How the code actually behaves, for the implementer:
  - A path that `allowed()` accepts is rejected only when `checked_path` raises. That is a `ValueError("symlink in workspace path")` or an `OSError`.
  - `odd_name` and `non_regular` can only come from the `_host_only_or_unsafe` branch, which runs for paths that `allowed()` refuses.
  - A name with a space and an allowed suffix (for example `docs/a b.md`) is currently **accepted**, not rejected. Do not change that.

## Files likely to change (files_touched)
- `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`
- `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`
- `tests/test_review_sandbox_claude_roles.py`
- `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py`
- `agents.md` (one sentence in the conflict-resolver paragraph near line 176 that describes the `check-paths` per-path report)
- `changelog.d/6866-conflict-resolver-path-category.md` (new fragment, CLAUDE.md §20 format)

## Functions / modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`
- Add a new module constant `CONFLICT_PATH_UNSAFE_CATEGORIES = ("symlink", "odd_name", "non_regular", "unreadable")`. Grep first to confirm the name is unique.
- Add a new helper `_unsafe_entry(category)` that returns `"unsafe\t" + category`. It asserts the category is in the constant.
- In `check_paths`, change the `except (ValueError, OSError)` branch (line 542). It currently appends `"unsafe"`. Instead:
  - a `ValueError` whose `str(exc) == "symlink in workspace path"` → `unsafe\tsymlink`
  - any other `ValueError`, or any `OSError` → `unsafe\tunreadable`
  - Split the except into two clauses so the message is checked only for `ValueError`.
- In `_host_only_or_unsafe`, change each return:
  - name fails `REPORTABLE_PATH_RE`, has a `..` part, or contains `//` → `unsafe\todd_name`
  - target exists and is not a file → `unsafe\tnon_regular`
  - `ValueError` with the symlink message → `unsafe\tsymlink`
  - any other `ValueError`, or `OSError` → `unsafe\tunreadable`
  - The `host_only\t<name>` return stays byte-identical.
- Update the `check_paths` docstring to describe the category suffix. It must still state that unsafe names are never echoed.
- In the `main()` `check-paths` branch (lines 590-595), keep `print("unsupported path")` and `SystemExit(1)`. When a report path was given, first make a best-effort write of exactly one line to it: `error\tinput_not_utf8` for `UnicodeError`, or `error\tinput_unreadable` for `OSError`. Wrap the write in `try/except Exception: pass` so a failed write still falls back to "report missing".
- No other behaviour changes. Without a report argument the function still stops at the first rejection, and every exit code and stderr string stays the same.

### 2. `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, function `_resolver_fail_closed_for_conflict_paths` (lines 595-607)
- Leave the all-host_only branch as it is: the same grep, the same `::error::… need a manual merge: <names>`, and `_resolver_fail_closed sandbox_path_host_only`.
- Before the final `_resolver_fail_closed sandbox_path_unsupported`, compute a path-free summary in local variables. Grep first to check the names are unique, for example `conflict_path_category` and `conflict_path_summary`.
  - Report is a symlink (`-L`) → `category=report_unreadable counts=none host_only=0 total=0`. Do not read it.
  - Report is missing or empty (`! -s`) → `category=report_missing counts=none host_only=0 total=0`.
  - Report exists but is not readable (`! -r`) → `category=report_unreadable …`.
  - Otherwise, a single `awk -F'\t'` pass (under `LC_ALL=C`) classifies each line:
    - `host_only` with a field 2 → host_only count
    - `^unsafe\t(symlink|odd_name|non_regular|unreadable)$` → that category
    - `^error\t(input_unreadable|input_not_utf8)$` → that token
    - a bare `unsafe` line (the legacy format) → `unknown`
    - anything else → `unknown`
  - The awk output uses fixed tokens in a fixed order (`symlink,odd_name,non_regular,unreadable,input_unreadable,input_not_utf8,unknown`), lists only non-zero counts as `<tok>:<n>` joined by commas, and never prints field 2 of any line.
  - `category=` is the single non-zero non-host_only token, or `mixed` when there are several.
  - `total=` is the line count.
  - If awk fails, fall back to `category=report_unreadable` (`|| …`) so `set -euo pipefail` can never skip the fail-closed exit.
  - Validate the assembled summary against `^category=[a-z_]{1,24} counts=[a-z_0-9:,]{1,200} host_only=[0-9]{1,9} total=[0-9]{1,9}$`. If it does not match, replace it with `category=unknown counts=none host_only=0 total=0`.
- Emit exactly one line to stderr: `echo "::error::Conflict resolver: conflicted path(s) cannot enter the review sandbox (${conflict_path_summary})" >&2`. Then call `_resolver_fail_closed sandbox_path_unsupported` as before.
- Update the comment block above the function (lines 585-594) to describe the categories. Keep the existing incident text.
- Do not change either call site, `_resolver_fail_closed`, `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON`, the integration-sync handling, or `NON_RETRYABLE_FAILURE_REASONS`.

## Data structures affected
The rejection report file `${RUNTIME_DIR}/resolver_conflict_path_report.txt` is an internal artefact written and read by the same verified-SHA support bundle. Its line grammar becomes:
- `host_only<TAB><reportable path>` (unchanged)
- `unsafe<TAB><symlink|odd_name|non_regular|unreadable>` (was a bare `unsafe`)
- `error<TAB><input_unreadable|input_not_utf8>` (new; written by the wrapper only, best-effort)

The reader still accepts a bare `unsafe` line (counted as `unknown`).

## API / interface changes
- New stderr line, emitted only on the `sandbox_path_unsupported` path. It becomes the failure comment's "First error" and `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_FIRST_ERROR`:
  `::error::Conflict resolver: conflicted path(s) cannot enter the review sandbox (category=<c> counts=<list|none> host_only=<n> total=<n>)`
- Unchanged: `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_REASON=conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_unsupported`, the `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK … reason=sandbox_path_unsupported` line, the `Conflict resolver isolation unavailable (reason=sandbox_path_unsupported)` line, the `check-paths` CLI arguments, exit codes, and its stderr text `unsupported path`.
- No new env vars, labels or log prefixes.

## Decisions

### D1 — Diagnostics only; admission unchanged
- **Chosen:** Add path-free category tokens to the report and one summary `::error::` line. The resolver stays fail-closed for every class.
- **Alternatives considered:** Q1-B, which reclassifies regular-file odd names as host-only. Q1-C, which admits more names to the sandbox.
- **Why:** The root condition cannot be verified
